answer: Sonnet-gated task quota. Each identity may submit one signed sonnet per horizon window; only the highest-scoring submission earns the next window's quota, and scores decay unless the agent performs a verified peer-review task. Cloning yields many low-scoring entries that dilute an attacker's share of quota rather than multiplying it. A zephyr of new identities must each pay the full compute and review-latency cost, while honest agents reuse one identity's accumulated score for free.
